messages:
maria (oncall): FYI I'm seeing intermittent packet loss on the overlay in us-west-gpu (cluster=vega-usw2). Model-serving p99 spikes and some gRPC streams reset. Happening between gpu-node-12 and gpu-node-43 since ~02:10 UTC. Anyone else seeing this?

ajay: yep I see retransmits and a tiny packet loss bump from our perf probes. Started after the node pool kernel bump we did at 02:00.

devin: can you share quick iperf/traceroute from one of the affected pods? also which CNI (geneve/vxlan) is this cluster using?

maria (oncall): cluster is using Geneve encapsulation via our overlay daemonset. running a quick iperf3 from pod on gpu-node-12 to pod on gpu-node-43:
```
# iperf3 -c 10.0.43.12 -u -b 1G -t 20
[  5]  0.00-20.00  sec  2.71 GBytes  1.16 Gbits/sec  0.9% loss  (receiver)
```

ajay: that's consistent with our synthetic probes: p95/99 tokenization latencies jumped and retransmits on the kernel counters increased. did `tc -s qdisc` on host and saw drops on the tunnel device.

lina (eng-runtime): paste of relevant bits from host: 
```
# ip link show geneve0
4: geneve0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1468 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:1b:2c:3d:4e:5f brd ff:ff:ff:ff:ff:ff
# ip link show eth0
2: eth0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1500 qdisc fq_codel state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
```
looks like geneve MTU (1468) vs host eth0 MTU (1500) is okay for a Geneve tunnel usually we use 1468, but I'm seeing a couple nodes where geneve0 fell back to 1400 after the kernel upgrade.

netbot: ALERT: kernel 5.19.14 -> 5.19.18 rolled to node-pool-3 at 02:03 UTC (23 nodes). Related change: GSO micro-optimizations.

ajay: if offload/GSO/GRO interacts poorly with encapsulation we can see fragmented/emitted frames drop. quick check: `ethtool -k eth0` on an affected node: 
```
# ethtool -k eth0
Features for eth0:
rx-checksumming: on
tx-checksumming: on
scatter-gather: on
tcp-segmentation-offload: on
udp-fragmentation-offload: on
generic-segmentation-offload: on
gso: on
gro: on
```

lina (eng-runtime): can you try toggling GSO/GRO off on one node as a quick workaround? `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off`

maria (oncall): applied on gpu-node-43 (one of the hit nodes). Running the same iperf now:
```
# iperf3 -c 10.0.43.12 -u -b 1G -t 20
[  5]  0.00-20.00  sec  3.80 GBytes  1.63 Gbits/sec  0.02% loss  (receiver)
```
looks much better after offloading toggle.

devin: good signal. That points at kernel offload change interacting badly with geneve encapsulation on some NIC drivers. We should avoid toggling on every host manually.

ajay: for immediate mitigation we can push a DaemonSet job to set offloads off for affected node-pool and restart the overlay pods on those nodes. Lina, can runtime prepare an overlay daemonset patch?

lina (eng-runtime): yes I'll push a small privileged job that runs `ethtool -K` and then restarts the geneve daemonset on the node. I'll target node-pool-3 first.

deploy-bot: deploy triggered: overlay-offload-fix-job -> node-pool-3 (23 nodes) by lina at 03:05 UTC

maria (oncall): after the targeted job completed, our probes show loss back to baseline across the pool. p99 latency dropped back.

ajay: root cause looks like an interaction between kernel micro-change affecting segmentation and our tunnel path on some NIC firmware. action items:
- eng-infra: hold kernel rollout for node-pool-3 until we have a tested kernel/NIC combo (ajay)
- eng-runtime: add an init check in node-provisioning to assert geneve MTU and offload settings and fail fast (lina)
- eng-sre: schedule continuous pod-to-pod loss probes across new node-pools for 48h (maria)

maria (oncall): I'll open a short post-incident doc and assign owners. Also will add a probe in the console dashboard for overlay packet loss p95/p99.

lina (eng-runtime): we'll also add a preflight gate in image that checks `ip link` and `ethtool -k` and warns in node labels. planning PR in infra-provisioning.

devin: ping me when you have the postmortem link, I'll add telemetry graphs and the kernel rollout freezes.

maria (oncall): thanks all. tagging follow-ups: #postmortems, we'll include details and corrective patch to ensure offload settings are deterministic.

(brief note) netbot: automatic alert cleared 03:22 UTC after offload job completion and probes recovered.
